issues.claim: Only a shared lock (`S`): transaction B can read the row as well. / Which request of transaction B is granted immediately
issues.problem: The word "only" is not true in SQL Server. An update (U) lock is also compatible with an existing S lock, as the fetched guide says: "U locks are compatible with S locks". Intent locks on higher levels are compatible too. The prompt asks about any request on the row, so a learner is taught that S is the only lock granted next to S. The generator notes admit U was dropped from the options only so that one answer stays correct, and the prompt never narrows the scope to S and X.
issues.suggestedFix: Restrict the prompt to the two basic modes, for example "Transaction B requests either a shared (S) or an exclusive (X) lock on the same row. Which request is granted immediately?". Then reword the options without "only": a) "The shared lock (S) request is granted at once, the exclusive lock (X) request waits." b) "The X request is granted at once, the S request waits." c) "Both are granted at once." d) "Both wait until A ends.". Apply the same change in ru: "Транзакция B запрашивает разделяемую (S) или монопольную (X) блокировку...". Add a sentence to the explanation that U is also compatible with S but is outside this question.

issues.claim: Can reading a row get in the way of another read of the same row? And of a change to that row?
issues.problem: The hint almost spells out the answer: reads do not block reads, and reads block changes. It is a strong nudge.
issues.suggestedFix: Make it weaker, for example: "Think about which operations can safely happen at the same time on one row and which cannot." Update the ru hint to match.

issues.claim: under `READ COMMITTED` the shared lock is released as soon as the read completes
issues.problem: This is true only for the default locking READ COMMITTED. With READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT ON, readers take no S locks. The guide excerpt supports the claim only for the locking variant.
issues.suggestedFix: Write "under the default locking READ COMMITTED (without READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT)" in both locales.

issues.claim: Both links are cited as support for "wrapping the indexed column in a function makes the predicate non-sargable, so the optimizer reads the whole index"
issues.problem: The excerpt of the index design guide covers clustered and nonclustered index structure and says nothing about functions on columns or sargability. The execution-plans overview excerpt is a generic description of plans and does not mention non-sargable predicates. The item shows no support for the central claim from either page. The generator notes raise the same doubt.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace or add a source that states the claim explicitly. Candidates are a Microsoft Learn page that covers SARGable predicates, or the Index Seek and Index Scan sections of the "Logical and physical showplan operator reference". Confirm the page text before citing it. Update linkTitles in both locales to match.

issues.claim: SELECT Id, CustomerId, Total ... The index is covering (`INCLUDE (CustomerId, Total)`)
issues.problem: The index is covering only if `Id` is the clustering key, because that is the only way it appears in the nonclustered index. The snippet never says so. Without it, the claim in the explanation that the plan uses the index as a full scan has no basis.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a comment to the code, e.g. "-- Id is the clustered primary key; CreatedAt is datetime2; dbo.Orders has millions of rows". Alternatively add Id to the INCLUDE list or say "the clustering key Id is carried in the index" in the explanation (both locales).

issues.claim: Compare the values the index is sorted by with what is actually compared to the number in the `WHERE` clause.
issues.problem: The hint comes close to giving the answer away: it points straight at the thing being compared in the WHERE clause.
issues.suggestedFix: Weaken it, e.g. "Which condition makes the engine compute something for every row before it can compare?"
